chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who forgot, so he ate and drank, then remembered,
he said: 'He does not break his fast; it is merely something Allah provided for him, so let him complete his fast.'
ai.seo_question: Does eating or drinking out of forgetfulness break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting nullifies the act of eating or drinking, distinguishing it from deliberate consumption, thereby preserving the validity of the fast without requiring expiation (kaffarah). This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for understanding the mercy inherent in divine law, as the individual is treated as if they were still fasting due to Allah's provision of sustenance. The hadith underscores the principle that minor lapses due to human error do not invalidate the spiritual intent of worship.
